title: Manipur steps up highway security after ambush kills four Naga civilians in Ukhrul
dek: Four civilians were shot dead on the Imphal-Ukhrul highway on Friday. Tangkhul Naga groups have given the state and the Centre three days to act, and the families say they will not claim the bodies until then.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Manipur's government has ordered every security post along the Imphal-Ukhrul highway to strengthen its cover and keep up combing operations, after suspected militants ambushed two vehicles on Friday and killed four Tangkhul Naga civilians, among them a woman and her son and a brother and sister.

Tangkhul Naga organisations have given the state and central governments three days to meet their demands, which include an investigation by the National Investigation Agency (NIA), and the families have said they will not claim the bodies until the demands are met, according to reports. The deadline runs out around Monday.

## What happened

The attack took place between noon and 1 pm on Friday, 13 November, near New Haven on National Highway 202, under Litan police station in Ukhrul district, police said, according to reports. Gunmen opened fire on two Imphal-bound vehicles, a car and a pick-up truck, and all four people inside died at the spot. Preliminary reports said the firing came from near Yaolen village. The site is a few hundred metres from a Border Security Force (BSF) outpost, Tangkhul Naga groups said.

The state government has described the attackers as unknown armed miscreants. Reports differ on who was responsible: most refer to suspected militants, while the Tangkhul Naga Long (TNL), the community's apex body, has blamed cadres of the Kuki National Army-Burma and the Village Volunteers of Eastern Zone. The Declaration could not find a public response from either group, and no arrests had been announced by Sunday evening.

On Saturday Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh chaired a security review, which decided to intensify area domination exercises, keep up round-the-clock patrols and have every post strengthen cover in its area, according to reports. Home Minister Govindas Konthoujam told reporters in Imphal on Sunday that operations were under way to catch those involved, but said it was not feasible to station security forces at every location in the state. He appealed for public cooperation and restraint.

## The demands

In a joint statement, the TNL and the Tangkhul Naga Foothills Organisation said the ambush "had eroded public trust in the existing security arrangements", according to reports. They demanded that alleged Kuki militants be removed from Naga-inhabited areas, that the NIA take over the case, and that the central security forces posted at New Haven be withdrawn. If the deadline passes, they warned of an indefinite agitation.

The groups said it was the fourth fatal incident at the same spot. One Naga MLA said nine people had been killed in as many months along a 15-km stretch of the highway, according to reports. The Coordinating Committee on Manipur Integrity, a Meitei civil society body, also condemned the killings and called for stronger highway security.

## Background

The ambush came a day after a 42-year-old Kuki woman was killed and two people were injured in firing near the border of Senapati and Kangpokpi districts on Thursday. On Saturday, suspected militants fired towards Khamsom, a Poumai Naga village in Senapati district, though no one was reported hurt.

Manipur has been in conflict since May 2023, when violence broke out between the Meitei and Kuki-Zo communities. Tensions between Naga and Kuki groups in the hill districts have grown alongside it. The TNL listed a series of recent incidents in Ukhrul and Kamjong districts this month, including an ambush on vehicles near Litan on 4 November and the wounding of a farmer by gunfire on 12 November. For people in Ukhrul, the violence has turned the road to Imphal, the state's main link to hospitals, markets and the airport, into a long and costly journey, with reports of detours of up to seven hours.

## What happens next

The three-day ultimatum expires around 16 November. The Naga groups have called on the wider Naga community to back protests if their demands are not met. The state government has not said whether it will seek an NIA investigation.
